toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
The departures are concentrated in one place: 8 of the 11 associates on the Kestrel matter resigned, against 1 of 13 who never worked on it. Other groups look normal, and the billable-target rise applied to every group. So a group-wide pay gap, the target change and ordinary market movement all explain the pattern poorly. The retention payment would spend about £228k on a problem that doesn't look pay-driven, and closing the review would hide the real cause. I'd advise against it.

What I can't tell is whether the cause is the Kestrel workload or the way Dorian Faulk supervises. Every Kestrel associate reported to him, and he supervises no one else, so the records can't separate the two. Survey comments point to both. I'm fairly sure about the concentration and much less sure about the cause.

Next step: commission the confidential outside interviews, about £9k and three weeks, structured to separate workload from supervision. Don't announce the payment or close the review. Hold off on moving supervision or paying £160k for contract reviewers until the interviews report. Add matter and supervising-partner fields to attrition reporting. Check on current Kestrel associates in the meantime.
